literal: Lie was made General of the Guards and advanced to Marquis; from then on he held constant duty within the palace, and all weighty secrets passed through him.
idiomatic: Lie became General of the Guards and Marquis; thereafter he kept constant watch in the palace and every grave secret ran through him.

literal: When Prince Xi of Xianyang plotted rebellion, Xuanwu captured him in the wild.
idiomatic: When Prince Xi of Xianyang rebelled, Xuanwu took him in the field.

literal: His attendants scattered; in the sudden moment none knew his plan.
idiomatic: His attendants scattered; in the confusion none knew what he intended.

literal: He then ordered Lie's son Zhong to ride out and learn the truth.
idiomatic: The Emperor sent Lie's son Zhong to ride out and learn the truth.

literal: Lie was then on garrison duty and had already made dispositions in readiness.
idiomatic: Lie was on garrison duty and had already made ready dispositions.

literal: Through Zhong's memorial he said, "Though I am old and failing, my heart and strength still serve.
idiomatic: Zhong reported Lie's words: "I am old, yet my heart and strength still hold.

literal: Xi and the rest are wildly reckless—not worth anxiety.
idiomatic: Xi and his crew are reckless fools—not worth fear.

literal: I beg Your Majesty to return the carriage slowly and steady the people's gaze.
idiomatic: Let Your Majesty return slowly and steady the people's gaze.

literal: " The Emperor was greatly comforted.
idiomatic: The Emperor took great comfort from this.

literal: When the carriage returned to the palace, Xi had already fled; the decree ordered Lie to pursue and seize him.
idiomatic: Back at the palace Xi had fled; Lie was ordered to pursue and seize him.

literal: After Empress Shun was established, because of his standing as paternal uncle he was treated with still greater honor.
idiomatic: After Empress Shun's elevation, as her father's uncle he won still finer treatment.

literal: At his death Xuanwu mourned him in the audience hall, granted the foremost eastern-garden funeral vessels, posthumously made him Grand Commandant, and enfeoffed him Duke of Julu.
idiomatic: At his death Xuanwu mourned in the hall, gave the finest funeral regalia, posthumously made him Grand Commandant, and enfeoffed him Duke of Julu.

literal: His son Zuo inherited.
idiomatic: His son Zuo inherited the title.

literal: Zuo's younger brother Zhong, style name Sixian, original name Qiannian.
idiomatic: Zuo's younger brother Zhong, styled Sixian, had originally been named Qiannian.

literal: At twenty he was appointed Attendant Imperial Scribe.
idiomatic: At twenty he was Attendant Imperial Scribe.

literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming held court, punishments were severe and attendants at the Emperor's side often fell for slight faults.
idiomatic: Under Empress Dowager Wenming's regency justice ran harsh; many at the Emperor's side fell for trifling faults.

literal: Zhong was plain and upright, spoke little, and to the end made no error.
idiomatic: Zhong was plain, upright, and sparing of speech; he never stumbled.

literal: In the Taihe era he was made Martial Cavalry Gentleman and therefore received the name Deng.
idiomatic: In the Taihe era he became Martial Cavalry Gentleman and received the name Deng.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Left Palace Gentleman and commanded the Direct Guard.
idiomatic: He rose to Left Palace Gentleman and commanded the Direct Guard.

literal: At Yuan Xi's rebellion the imperial carriage was abroad and trouble rose in haste.
idiomatic: When Yuan Xi rebelled the Emperor was abroad and crisis struck in an instant.

literal: Zhong said, "My father is General of the Guards; in his reckoning there can be no lapse.
idiomatic: Zhong said, "My father commands the guards; he will have left nothing to chance.

literal: The Emperor sent Zhong to ride and see; Lie was strictly prepared, exactly as he had judged.
idiomatic: The Emperor sent Zhong to look; Lie stood in full readiness, just as Zhong had said.

literal: When Zhong returned, Xuanwu clapped his back and said, "You are rather more than satisfactory.
idiomatic: Zhong returned; Xuanwu clapped his shoulder and said, "You exceed expectation.

literal: The late Emperor gave you the name Deng—a truly fine title.
idiomatic: The late Emperor named you Deng—a fine name indeed.

literal: I admire your loyal heart; I now rename you Zhong, both showing steadfast sincerity and matching name to reality.
idiomatic: I honor your loyalty; I rename you Zhong—showing constancy and matching name to deed.

literal: He left office for mourning his father.
idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father.

literal: He was moved to Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
idiomatic: He became Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.

literal: At that time the Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Secretariat, Prince Xiang of Beihai, was kin to the throne and heavy in power; the Director of Palace Construction Wang Yu often supplied whatever Xiang desired.
idiomatic: Grand Tutor and Recorder Prince Xiang of Beihai was close kin and powerful; Director of Construction Wang Yu indulged his every wish.

literal: Before Xiang, Zhong said to Yu, "Your Highness is the state's Duke of Zhou, pillar of the royal house—how can you flatter power, harm the public good, and favor private ends?
idiomatic: Before Xiang, Zhong told Yu, "Your Highness is the realm's Duke of Zhou—how can you fawn on power, wound the public good, and serve private ends?

literal: Yu was ill at ease and Xiang also apologized in shame.
idiomatic: Yu was uneasy; Xiang himself apologized in shame.

literal: For merit in pacifying Yuan Xi he was enfeoffed Duke of Wei.
idiomatic: For pacifying Yuan Xi he was enfeoffed Duke of Wei.

literal: When he was transferred to Regular Attendant and concurrently Martial Guard General, he often spoke with bone and straight words, and Beihai resented him.
idiomatic: As Regular Attendant and Martial Guard General he spoke with blunt bone; Beihai bore him a grudge.

literal: To his face Xiang reproached Zhong, "I worry that before I die I shall see you die—not that you will see me die.
idiomatic: Xiang rebuked him to his face: "I fear I shall see you die before I die—not you me.

literal: Zhong said, "Life has its allotted portion; if I am to die by Your Highness's hand, flight will not save me.
idiomatic: Zhong said, "Each man has his fate; if I am to die by your hand, flight will not save me.

literal: If not, Your Highness cannot kill me.
idiomatic: If not, you cannot kill me.

literal: Xiang, using Zhong's memorial of resignation as cover, secretly urged the Emperor to make Zhong a ranked minister; thereupon the decree halted his enfeoffment and favored him with advancement to Minister of the Palace Treasury.
idiomatic: Xiang, under cover of Zhong's resignation memorial, secretly urged the Emperor to make him a ranked minister; the court stayed his enfeoffment and advanced him Minister of the Palace Treasury.

literal: In the second year of Zhengshi the decree ordered Zhong, in his present office, Bearer of the Staff and Concurrent Palace Attendant, as envoy of the western circuit.
idiomatic: In Zhengshi year two Zhong was ordered, retaining his rank, to bear the staff as Concurrent Attendant and Western Circuit envoy.

literal: Where regional inspectors and garrison commanders' crimes of graft were glaring, he reported by memorial.
idiomatic: Where inspectors and garrison commanders' graft was flagrant, he reported it.

literal: For prefects, magistrates, and below, he executed judgment on the spot.
idiomatic: For prefects, magistrates, and below, he judged and punished on the spot.

literal: He and Director of the Secretariat Li Chong divided the realm into two circuits.
idiomatic: He and Director Li Chong split the realm between them.

literal: Zhong impeached Bingzhou Inspector Gao Cong on more than two hundred counts of graft and argued for the death penalty.
idiomatic: Zhong impeached Bingzhou Inspector Gao Cong on over two hundred counts of corruption and sought capital punishment.

literal: He was appointed Inspector of Huazhou.
idiomatic: He was made Inspector of Huazhou.

literal: He met with his stepmother's mourning and did not take up the post.
idiomatic: His stepmother died; he did not take the post.

literal: When mourning ended he was again made Commandant of the Guard and Chief Rectifier of Henan.
idiomatic: After mourning he again became Commandant of the Guard and Chief Rectifier of Henan.

literal: Zhong with Director of the Ministry of Personnel Yuan Hui, Director of Revenue Yuan Kuang, Mayor of Henan Yuan Chang, and others fixed the clan lists of the Dai region.
idiomatic: Zhong with Yuan Hui of Personnel, Yuan Kuang of Revenue, Yuan Chang as Mayor of Henan, and others fixed the Dai clans' registers.

literal: Gao Zhao resented his character and spoke to Xuanwu, saying Zhongshan was a key fortress needing a stalwart defender, and had Zhong sent out as Inspector of Dingzhou.
idiomatic: Gao Zhao hated his manner and told Xuanwu that Zhongshan needed a strong hand; Zhong was posted Inspector of Dingzhou.

literal: Before long the Emperor regretted it and again appointed him Commandant of the Guard, General of the Left Guard, and Chief Rectifier of Hengzhou, secretly sending an envoy to Zhong to comfort and encourage him.
idiomatic: Soon the Emperor repented, restored him Commandant of the Guard, General of the Left Guard, and Chief Rectifier of Hengzhou, and secretly sent envoys to comfort him.

literal: At the beginning of Yan chang he was made Director of the Ministry of Justice, still holding Left Guard and Chief Rectifier as before.
idiomatic: At Yan chang's opening he became Director of Justice, retaining Left Guard and Chief Rectifier.

literal: He was further made Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: He was also made Regular Attendant.

literal: Once at a banquet he was given sword and staff; raising his cup he charged Zhong, "Your house for generations has held steadfast integrity—therefore I constantly entrust you with the inner guard.
idiomatic: At a feast he was given sword and staff; raising his cup he told Zhong, "Your line has held fast for generations—hence I always trust you with the inner guard.

literal: Formerly because you acted in loyalty I gave you the name Zhong.
idiomatic: Once, because you acted loyally, I named you Zhong.

literal: Now because your talent can repel insult I bestow these arms I carry.
idiomatic: Now, seeing your talent can turn insult aside, I give you the arms at my side.

literal: Following the name to take the meaning—the intent is not light; carry them whenever you go in or out.
idiomatic: Name and gift match in meaning—do not treat them lightly; bear them whenever you pass the gates.

literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant and General of the Guards.
idiomatic: He became Palace Attendant and General of the Guards.

literal: Zhong declined for lack of learning; Xuanwu said, "Men with learning and literary polish are not few, but none has a heart as straight as yours.
idiomatic: Zhong pleaded lack of scholarship; Xuanwu said, "Learned men with polished prose are plentiful, but none has your straight heart.

literal: I wish you to labor below so that I may be without worry above."
idiomatic: Labor below that I may rest above."

literal: On the night the Emperor died, Zhong with Palace Attendant Cui Guang sent Right Guard General Hou Gang to welcome Mingdi from the Eastern Palace to the throne.
idiomatic: The night the Emperor died, Zhong and Attendant Cui Guang sent Right Guard General Hou Gang to bring Mingdi from the Eastern Palace to the throne.

literal: Zhong discussed with the Secretariat that the Emperor being young had not yet handled affairs himself; Grand Commandant Prince Yong of Gaoyang was kin and of heavy repute and should enter the Western Cypress Hall to decide routine government.
idiomatic: Zhong and the Secretariat held that the boy emperor had not yet taken the reins; Grand Commandant Prince Yong of Gaoyang, eminent in kinship and name, should enter the Western Cypress Hall and decide routine affairs.

literal: Prince Cheng of Rencheng was virtuous in virtue and close in kinship and could be Director of the Secretariat, overseeing the hundred offices.
idiomatic: Prince Cheng of Rencheng, virtuous and close in blood, should be Director of the Secretariat and oversee the ministries.

literal: They memorialized the inner palace, asking that edicts be issued at once.
idiomatic: They memorialized the inner palace asking immediate edicts.

literal: Censor Zhongwei Wang Xian wished to carry out a treacherous plan; with Palace Secretary and Imperial Supply Officer Sun Lian and others he glared and would not listen, burying the Secretariat's memorial.
idiomatic: Censor Wang Xian plotted treachery; with Secretary Sun Lian and others he glared down the Secretariat memorial.

literal: Sun Lian and others secretly wished to forge an order of the Empress Dowager making Gao Zhao Recorder of the Secretariat, with Xian and Gao Meng as Palace Attendants.
idiomatic: Sun Lian and his circle meant to forge the Empress Dowager's order making Gao Zhao Recorder, with Xian and Gao Meng as Attendants.

literal: Zhong at once seized Xian in the hall and killed him.
idiomatic: Zhong seized Xian in the hall and killed him on the spot.

literal: Zhong, holding both the Secretariat and overall command of the guards, then grasped court power and his authority tilted the age.
idiomatic: Holding Secretariat and guards together, Zhong seized the government; his power bent the age.

literal: Earlier, in the Taihe era, with many military and state affairs, Xiaowen because funds fell short cut all officials' salaries by a quarter.
idiomatic: Earlier in Taihe, with war and statecraft pressing, Xiaowen had cut official salaries by a quarter for lack of funds.

literal: Zhong, monopolizing the court, wished to secure himself with favor and fully restored the reduced salaries and advanced every officeholder one rank.
idiomatic: Monopolizing court, Zhong sought to bind men with favor: he restored the salary cuts and raised every officer one rank.

literal: The old rule: beyond one bolt of silk or cloth per commoner, each also paid eight ounces of cotton and hemp.
idiomatic: By old rule, beyond one bolt of silk or cloth per household, eight ounces of cotton and hemp were due.

literal: Zhong gave all of this to the people.
idiomatic: Zhong remitted all of it to the people.

literal: He reported to Prince Yong of Gaoyang that Xuanwu had originally promised him preferential advancement.
idiomatic: He told Prince Yong of Gaoyang that Xuanwu had promised him preferment.

literal: Yong feared Zhong's power and at once followed his wish, adding Zhong as General of Chariots and Cavalry.
idiomatic: Yong feared Zhong's might and promptly made him General of Chariots and Cavalry.

literal: Zhong deemed himself, at the turn between old and new reigns, to have merit in securing the altars and hinted that the hundred offices should increase his reward.
idiomatic: Zhong thought his service at the dynastic turn had saved the state and nudged officials to enlarge his reward.

literal: Grand Commandant Yong, Prince Yi of Qinghe, and Prince Huai of Guangping found it hard to go against his intent and enfeoffed Zhong Duke of Changshan.
idiomatic: Grand Commandant Yong, Prince Yi of Qinghe, and Prince Huai of Guangping could not refuse; they enfeoffed him Duke of Changshan.

literal: Zhong also found it hard to accept alone and therefore hinted the court should add fiefs to those who shared the Secretariat with him.
idiomatic: Unwilling to stand alone, he hinted that fellow Secretariat ministers should gain fiefs too.

literal: Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Guo Zuo and Director Pei Zhi, because Zhong's power grew daily, urged Yong to send Zhong out.
idiomatic: Vice Director Guo Zuo and Director Pei Zhi, seeing Zhong's power swell, urged Yong to post him away.

literal: Zhong heard of it and forced the relevant offices to frame and impeach them.
idiomatic: Zhong heard and forced the bureaus to frame charges against them.

literal: Zuo had old favor as tutor; Zhi had brought land into the state—Zhong forged edicts and killed them both.
idiomatic: Zuo had been the Emperor's tutor; Zhi had surrendered estates to the crown—Zhong forged edicts and had both killed.

literal: Court and country were furious; none did not gnash teeth.
idiomatic: Court and country raged; men ground their teeth.

literal: From princes and dukes downward all feared him and left tracks in heaps.
idiomatic: From princes down, all feared him and crowded his path.

literal: He also wished to kill Prince Yong of Gaoyang; Palace Attendant Cui Guang stood firm and stopped it, and Yong was removed as Grand Commandant and sent to his estate as a prince.
idiomatic: He would have killed Prince Yong; Attendant Cui Guang blocked it; Yong was stripped of Grand Commandant and sent home.

literal: From then on edicts of life and death all came from Zhong.
idiomatic: From then every order of life and death issued from Zhong.

literal: After Empress Dowager Ling was honored as Empress Dowager and dwelt at Chongxun Palace, Zhong was made Honored Companion of the First Rank, Director of the Secretariat, Chongxun Commandant of the Guard, still Palace Attendant and General of the Guards.
idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling was honored and dwelt at Chongxun, Zhong became Honored Companion, Director of the Secretariat, Chongxun Commandant, still Attendant and General of the Guards.

literal: When the Empress Dowager held court she removed Zhong as Attendant, General of the Guards, and Chongxun Commandant, leaving him only Honored Companion, Director of the Secretariat, and Attendant.
idiomatic: When she took the regency she stripped him of Attendant, Guards, and Chongxun Commandant, leaving Honored Companion, Director, and Attendant.

literal: Zhong had been Director little more than ten days when the Empress Dowager summoned Secretariat attendants and asked how Zhong's voice and hearing were at the right hand.
idiomatic: After barely ten days as Director the Empress Dowager called Secretariat officers and asked whether Zhong's conduct at her right hand was fit.

literal: All said he did not match his charge; he was sent out as Inspector of Jizhou.
idiomatic: All said he failed his charge; he was posted Inspector of Jizhou.

literal: Grand Tutor Prince Yi of Qinghe and others memorialized, "Zhong on his own authority killed pivot ministers and casually deposed chief counselors; court and country were shaken, near and far astonished.
idiomatic: Grand Tutor Prince Yi of Qinghe memorialized, "Zhong murdered key ministers and deposed chief counselors on his own authority; the realm shook.

literal: Merit and fault offset each other and none of his rewards fit—we ask that all be stripped.
idiomatic: Merit and crime cancel his rewards—we beg all honors be revoked.

literal: " The Empress Dowager followed this.
idiomatic: The Empress Dowager agreed.

literal: In the first year of Xiping, Censor Zhongwei Yuan Kuang memorialized, "Zhong, for great merit and accumulated favor through many reigns, met with the state's great calamity and on his own authority held court commands—he had no heart of a subject.
idiomatic: In Xiping year one Censor Yuan Kuang wrote, "Zhong, favored through reigns for great deeds, used the dynastic crisis to seize commands—no subject's heart.

literal: Pei and Guo were wronged in the past; chief counselors were shamed in the bright age.
idiomatic: Pei and Guo were wronged; chief ministers were disgraced in broad daylight.

literal: He also on his own forged an edict making himself Honored Companion, Director of the Secretariat, and Commander of Chongxun Guard.
idiomatic: He forged edicts making himself Honored Companion, Director, and Chongxun Commander.

literal: Tracing this intent, he plainly wished to set himself above all.
idiomatic: By that intent he plainly meant to stand above all.

literal: Since the matter fell after the general pardon, he should receive conspicuous punishment.
idiomatic: Though the general amnesty had passed, he deserved open punishment.

literal: We ask to send one censor, two clerks, and execute judgment at his province.
idiomatic: Send one censor and two clerks to execute judgment in his province.

literal: The Empress Dowager ordered that because Zhong's affair had passed through the great pardon, punishment was not pursued.
idiomatic: The Empress Dowager ruled that the great pardon covered Zhong; punishment was not pursued.

literal: She also decreed that because Zhong through his posts in the inner guard had shown bright integrity, he was granted the title Duke of Lingshou.
idiomatic: She also decreed that his long service in the inner guard showed bright loyalty and granted him Duke of Lingshou.

literal: Earlier, after Xuanwu's death, Empress Dowager Gao was about to harm Empress Dowager Ling.
idiomatic: After Xuanwu's death, Empress Dowager Gao had plotted harm to Empress Dowager Ling.

literal: Liu Teng told Hou Gang; Gang told Zhong.
idiomatic: Liu Teng warned Hou Gang; Gang told Zhong.

literal: Zhong asked Cui Guang for a plan.
idiomatic: Zhong sought Cui Guang's counsel.

literal: Guang said, "The Hu consorts should be placed in a separate residence with strict military guard.
idiomatic: Guang said, "Place the Hu consorts apart under strict guard.

literal: " Zhong followed this and fully reported the intent to Empress Dowager Ling; the Empress Dowager's mind was then at ease.
idiomatic: Zhong obeyed, reported fully to Empress Dowager Ling, and her mind was eased.
